pos.personaBrief: Hungary dominated possession (Olympic final, Wembley 35 shots, England unable to get the ball) and built through short passing with Bozsik and Hidegkuti; it did not cede the ball to counter.

pro.personaBrief: Short passing with sweeper-keeper Grosics starting play and a mix of short and long passes (Nemzeti Sport, FA Year Book), with fast, rotating forward movement and a roaming Bozsik taking risks.

est.personaBrief: Hidegkuti and Hungary's forwards constantly interchanged ('where we lined up at kick-off was irrelevant'), with a deep-lying centre-forward and no fixed positions (Buzanszky).

lar.personaBrief: Wingers tucked in to support the inside forwards and the play ran through Hidegkuti, Puskas and Kocsis in the middle, with Czibor and Budai cutting back rather than only crossing.

blo.personaBrief: Sweeper-keeper and a high line let the team play in the opponent's half, but the evidence of active pressing is thin and Grosics recalled dropping off rather than pressing at Wembley.

mar.personaBrief: Defence was WM-style with individual duties (Lantos v Matthews, Lantos leaving Rahn free, FA Year Book 'same defensive tactics'); no source says zonal.

pla.personaBrief: Sebes imposed his system but also prepared for opponents (warm-ups imitating their tactics, the English ball, Wembley talk), while changing little of the identity.

res.personaBrief: The Golden Team played attacking, stylish football ('done it in style') with five forwards and is remembered despite the 1954 final loss; it never played for draws.

sis.personaBrief: Socialist football and collectivism: work shared out, everyone attacks and defends, with stars like Puskas bound into a rotating system but allowed to read the game.

jog.personaBrief: Technical, ball-playing team (Matthews praised ball control, passing), with a deep playmaker like Hidegkuti and rigorous fitness training (swimming, outrunning opponents).

bas.personaBrief: A fixed XI from Honved and MTK with continuity and experience over years; not academy-driven, and development was not the goal.

lid.personaBrief: Sebes was an undisputed leader with strict timetables and discipline, but held long tactical discussions that included Puskas and others.
